title: Definition of a trade
summary: A trade is an assignment of a Player Contract via a negotiated exchange between two or more Teams following an NBA trade call; waiver assignments are not trades.
detail_paraphrase: Under this Agreement a trade of a player means assigning a Player Contract pursuant to a negotiated exchange between two or more Teams that follows a trade conference call with the NBA league office. Assigning a player through the NBA waiver procedures is expressly not a trade.
conditions: Negotiated exchange between two or more Teams
Trade conference call with the NBA league office must precede the assignment
exceptions: Assignment of a player via waiver procedures is not a trade

title: Cash limit in trades (5.15% of Salary Cap)
summary: Across all trades in a Salary Cap Year, a Team may pay or receive at most 5.15% of the Salary Cap in cash, including cash reimbursement of acquired players' compensation.
detail_paraphrase: Subject to Section 2(e), in connection with one or more trades during a Salary Cap Year a Team may pay or receive, directly or indirectly, cash up to an aggregate equal to 5.15% of that year's Salary Cap across all such trades, counting cash received as reimbursement for compensation owed to acquired players. If a contract is signed and traded under Section 8(e)(1) and contains a signing bonus, payment of that bonus by the signing Team is treated as reimbursement subject to this limit. Amounts paid and received are not netted against each other, so paying the full limit in one trade exhausts the ability to pay, and receiving the full limit exhausts the ability to receive, in later trades that year.
conditions: One or more trades during the same Salary Cap Year
Cash paid and cash received are tracked separately and not netted
thresholds: 5.15% of the Salary Cap for the Salary Cap Year, aggregated across all trades; paid and received amounts counted separately
notes: Cross-reference: subject to apron rules in Section 2(e) (aprons bucket).

title: Consent required to trade a one-year QFA/EQFA contract (implicit no-trade)
summary: A player (non Two-Way) on a one-year contract who would become a Qualifying or Early Qualifying Veteran Free Agent at its end cannot be traded without his consent, unless the consent right was eliminated at signing.
detail_paraphrase: A player other than a Two-Way Player on a one-year Contract (excluding any Option Year) who would be a Qualifying Veteran Free Agent or Early Qualifying Veteran Free Agent upon completing that Contract may not be traded without his consent. Under Article II, Section 3(h), the player and Team may agree at signing to eliminate this consent right. If the player consents (or the right was eliminated) and is traded—except where a second-year Option was exercised before the trade—then for determining his free-agent status with the assignee Team he is treated as having changed Teams by signing as a Free Agent rather than by trade. For a player who did not eliminate the right at signing, the consent right continues for the initial trade and any subsequent proposed trade during the Contract term (excluding any Option Year).
conditions: Player is not a Two-Way Player
One-year Contract excluding any Option Year
Player would be a Qualifying Veteran Free Agent or Early Qualifying Veteran Free Agent at the end of the Contract
exceptions: Consent right eliminated at signing per Article II, Section 3(h)
Second-year Option exercised prior to the trade (changes the free-agent-status treatment)

title: No trade after the deadline in a contract's final season
summary: A Team cannot trade a player after the NBA trade deadline in the last season of his contract, or after the deadline in any season that could be the last based on an Option or Early Termination Option.
detail_paraphrase: A Team may not trade a player after the NBA trade deadline occurring in the last Season of the player's Contract, or after the trade deadline in any Season that could be the last Season of the Contract depending on whether an Option or Early Termination Option is exercised.
conditions: Trade attempted after the NBA trade deadline in the contract's final season (or a possible final season due to an Option/ETO)

title: 30-day trade restriction for draft rookies and Two-Way signings
summary: A Draft Rookie signing a Standard NBA Contract, or a player signing a Two-Way Contract, cannot be traded until 30 days after signing.
detail_paraphrase: No Draft Rookie who signs a Standard NBA Contract, and no player who signs a Two-Way Contract, may be traded before 30 days following the date the Contract is signed.
conditions: Draft Rookie signing a Standard NBA Contract, or a player signing a Two-Way Contract
thresholds: 30 days following the date the Contract is signed

title: Three-month / December 15 restriction for newly signed free agents
summary: A free agent signing a Standard NBA Contract cannot be traded until the later of three months after signing or December 15 of that Salary Cap Year.
detail_paraphrase: A player who signs a Standard NBA Contract as a Free Agent (or who signs a Standard NBA Contract while under a Two-Way Contract) may not be traded before the later of (A) three months after the Contract was signed or (B) December 15 of the Salary Cap Year in which it was signed. If the Contract was signed in connection with an agreement to trade it under Section 8(e), this rule does not apply to the initial trade but does apply if the Contract is traded a second time. A Two-Way Contract converted to a Standard NBA Contract under its conversion option is treated as a Standard NBA Contract signed by a Free Agent on the conversion date.
conditions: Player signs a Standard NBA Contract as a Free Agent, or signs a Standard NBA Contract while under a Two-Way Contract
exceptions: Contract signed in connection with a Section 8(e) sign-and-trade: rule applies only to a second trade, not the initial trade
thresholds: Later of three months after signing or December 15 of the Salary Cap Year

title: Three-month / January 15 restriction for re-signed Bird FAs with >120% raise on a capped team
summary: A QFA/EQFA re-signing with his prior over-the-cap team at more than 120% of his prior salary cannot be traded until the later of three months after signing or January 15.
detail_paraphrase: Notwithstanding the December 15 rule, a player re-signing a Standard NBA Contract with his prior Team may not be traded before the later of three months after signing or January 15 of that Salary Cap Year when both: the Team's Team Salary is above the Salary Cap immediately after the signing, and the player is a Qualifying or Early Qualifying Veteran Free Agent who, under Section 6(b)(1) or (3), signs a new Contract whose first-season Salary exceeds 120% of the Salary for the last season of his immediately prior Contract. This does not apply if the new Contract is for the Minimum Player Salary with no bonuses. If the prior Contract was a one-year minimum-salary deal (no bonuses), the prior Salary includes any portion of the minimum reimbursed from the League-wide benefits fund.
conditions: Team Salary above the Salary Cap immediately after the signing
Player is a Qualifying or Early Qualifying Veteran Free Agent re-signing with his prior Team under Section 6(b)(1) or (3)
New first-season Salary exceeds 120% of the last-season Salary of the prior Contract
exceptions: New Contract is for the Minimum Player Salary with no bonuses of any kind
thresholds: Later of three months after signing or January 15; trigger is first-season salary > 120% of prior last-season salary

title: Sign-and-trade of a Veteran Free Agent (Section 8(e)(1))
summary: A Veteran Free Agent and his Prior Team may sign a contract for the purpose of trading it, only under strict conditions on roster status, length, exception used, protection, timing, max salary, and the acquiring team's room.
detail_paraphrase: Subject to Section 2(e), a Veteran Free Agent and his Prior Team may enter a Player Contract pursuant to an agreement with another Team to sign and then trade the Contract, but only if all of the following hold: the player finished the prior Season on the Prior Team's roster; the Contract is at least three Seasons but no more than four Seasons (excluding any Option Year); it is not signed using the Non-Taxpayer Mid-Level or Room Mid-Level exception; the first Season is fully protected for lack of skill; it is entered into before the first day of the Regular Season; for a 5th Year Eligible Player meeting a Higher Max Criterion, Salary plus Unlikely Bonuses may not exceed 25% of the Salary Cap; and the acquiring Team has Room for the first-season Salary plus any Unlikely Bonuses.
conditions: Player finished the prior Season on the Prior Team's roster
Contract is 3 to 4 Seasons long excluding any Option Year
First Season fully protected for lack of skill
Signed before the first day of the Regular Season
Acquiring Team has Room for the first-season Salary plus Unlikely Bonuses
exceptions: Cannot be signed using the Non-Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception or the Mid-Level Salary Exception for Room Teams
5th Year Eligible Player meeting Higher Max Criteria capped at 25% of the Salary Cap
depends_on_terms: Mid-Level Salary Exception for Room Teams
thresholds: 3-4 seasons (excl. Option Year); 25% of Salary Cap cap for qualifying 5th Year Eligible Players
notes: Cross-reference: subject to apron rules in Section 2(e) (aprons bucket).

title: Sign-and-trade of a contract amendment / extension (Section 8(e)(2))
summary: A player and Team may amend or extend a contract for the purpose of trading it, subject to a blackout window and limits on extension length (3 seasons pre-2024-25, 4 seasons after).
detail_paraphrase: A player and his Team may amend a Player Contract (including by Extension but not by Renegotiation) under an agreement with another Team to sign the amendment and then trade the amended Contract, provided that: no such agreement may be made during the period from the last day of the last Regular Season covered by the Contract (or any Regular Season that could be the last based on an Option or ETO) through the following June 30; an Extension under this provision signed before the first day of the 2024-25 Salary Cap Year may cover at most three Seasons from signing; and one signed on or after that date may cover at most four Seasons. First-year Salary/Unlikely Bonuses and annual increases/decreases are governed by Section 7(a)(3)(iii) and Section 5(a)(4).
conditions: Amendment is an Extension (not a Renegotiation)
Agreement to sign-and-trade the amended Contract with another Team
exceptions: No such agreement during the period from the last day of the last covered Regular Season through the following June 30
thresholds: Max 3 Seasons (Extensions before 2024-25 Salary Cap Year) or 4 Seasons (on/after) from signing

title: No Exhibit 6 in a sign-and-trade contract or extension
summary: A contract or extension entered under Section 8(e)(1) or (2) may not contain an Exhibit 6, though the trade may be made conditional on passing a physical.
detail_paraphrase: A Player Contract or Extension entered into under Section 8(e)(1) or (2) may not include an Exhibit 6. However, the involved Teams may still agree that the trade—and thus the validity of the Contract or Extension—will be conditional on the player passing a physical examination performed by a physician designated by the assignee Team under NBA procedures.
conditions: Contract or Extension entered under Section 8(e)(1) or (2)
exceptions: Trade may be conditioned on passing an assignee-Team physical examination

title: Six-month trade restriction after large extension or renegotiation
summary: After a large 5-season (or pre-2024-25, 4+ season) extension or a renegotiation, a player cannot be traded for six months; an acquiring team likewise cannot give such an extension/renegotiation for six months after acquiring the player.
detail_paraphrase: If a player enters an Extension under Section 7(a) (other than a Designated Veteran Player Extension) that covers five Seasons (or, for Extensions before the 2024-25 Salary Cap Year, four or more Seasons) and/or provides Salary/Unlikely Bonuses or annual changes exceeding what was permissible in a Section 8(e)(2) sign-and-trade Extension at the time, or enters a Renegotiation under Section 7(c), the player may not be traded for six months after signing. Conversely, for six months after acquiring a player in a trade, the acquiring Team may not enter such an Extension or a Renegotiation with that player.
conditions: Extension under Section 7(a) covering 5 seasons (or 4+ before 2024-25) and/or exceeding the 8(e)(2) permissible amounts
Or a Renegotiation under Section 7(c)
exceptions: Designated Veteran Player Extensions governed separately under subsection (f)(ii)
thresholds: Six months following the Extension/Renegotiation signing, or six months following the trade for the acquiring Team

title: One-year trade restriction after a Designated Veteran Player Extension or Contract
summary: A player who signs a Designated Veteran Player Extension or Designated Veteran Player Contract cannot be traded for one year.
detail_paraphrase: If a player enters a Designated Veteran Player Extension under Section 7(a)(3)(ii) or a Designated Veteran Player Contract under Article II, Section 7, he may not be traded for one year after entering that Extension or Contract.
conditions: Player signs a Designated Veteran Player Extension or Designated Veteran Player Contract
thresholds: One year following the signing of the Designated Veteran Player Extension or Contract

title: Room calculation when trading an extended Rookie Scale Contract
summary: When trading an extended Rookie Scale Contract before the next Salary Cap Year, the acquiring team's Room is measured using the average of the last original-term salary and the extended-term salaries.
detail_paraphrase: If a Rookie Scale Contract is extended under Section 7(b) and a Team proposes to trade it before the first day of the Salary Cap Year immediately following the Extension, then, solely for determining whether the acquiring Team has Room, the Salary for the last Salary Cap Year of the original term is deemed equal to the average of the aggregate Salaries for that year and each year of the extended term. Special assumptions apply where the extended term's Base Compensation is expressed as a percentage of the Salary Cap (assume the Cap grows to 104.5% of the Cap at the time of the trade and the player meets no Higher Max Criteria in his fourth Rookie Scale season) or exceeds the applicable Maximum Annual Salary under that 104.5% assumption (use the deemed-amendment result).
conditions: Rookie Scale Contract extended under Section 7(b)
Proposed trade before the first day of the Salary Cap Year immediately following the Extension
thresholds: Deemed Cap growth assumption of 104.5% of the Salary Cap at the time of the proposed trade

title: Assignor cannot re-sign a player waived by the assignee for one year
summary: If a traded player is waived by the team that acquired him, the original team cannot re-sign or claim him until the earlier of one year after the trade closed or the July 1 after his contract's last season.
detail_paraphrase: If a Team trades a player and the assignee Team later places him on waivers, the assignor Team may not sign the player to a new Contract (or claim him off waivers) before the earlier of: one year after all conditions to the trade were satisfied; or the July 1 following the last Season of the player's Contract.
conditions: Player was traded, then waived by the assignee Team
Assignor Team seeks to re-sign or claim the player
thresholds: Earlier of one year after trade conditions satisfied, or July 1 following the last Season of the Contract

title: Divestment of preexisting financial arrangements before assignment
summary: Before a contract is assigned, the assignor team and the player must unwind any preexisting financial arrangements between them, except earned compensation and loans.
detail_paraphrase: Before any Player Contract is assigned, the assigning Team and the player must divest themselves, on mutually agreeable terms, of any preexisting financial arrangements between them. This does not apply to Compensation earned by the player before the assignment or to loans.
conditions: A Player Contract is about to be assigned and preexisting financial arrangements exist between the Team and player
exceptions: Compensation earned before the assignment
Loans

title: NBA must summarize trade terms to the Players Association
summary: Within one week of each trade, the NBA emails the Players Association a summary of the trade's principal terms, with limited confidentiality redactions.
detail_paraphrase: As soon as practicable after each trade, and no later than one week from the trade date, the NBA emails the Players Association a summary of the trade's principal terms. The NBA may omit terms it or involved Teams reasonably deem confidential, except any terms necessary to verify compliance with the Section 8(a) cash limit.
conditions: A trade has occurred
exceptions: Confidential terms may be omitted, except those needed to verify Section 8(a) cash-limit compliance
thresholds: No later than one week from the date of the trade

title: Standard Traded Player Exception (100% + $250,000, non-aggregated)
summary: A team over the cap can replace one Traded Player with replacement contracts totaling up to 100% of the traded player's pre-trade salary plus $250,000, acquired simultaneously or non-simultaneously within one year.
detail_paraphrase: Subject to Sections 2(e), 6(n), and 6(j)(6), a Team may use the Standard Traded Player Exception to replace one Traded Player with one or more Replacement Players acquired simultaneously or non-simultaneously, whose post-assignment Salaries for the Salary Cap Year of acquisition total no more than 100% of the Traded Player's pre-trade Salary plus $250,000. Any contract acquired non-simultaneously under this exception must be acquired within one year of the date the Traded Player was traded.
conditions: Single Traded Player (non-aggregated)
Team meets the Section 6(n) over/near-cap eligibility test
Non-simultaneous replacement acquired within one year of the trade
thresholds: Up to 100% of pre-trade Salary plus $250,000; non-simultaneous window of one year
notes: Cross-reference: $250,000 allowance reduced to $0 if post-assignment Apron Team Salary exceeds the First Apron Level (TRADE-029); subject to Section 2(e) apron rules (aprons bucket).

title: Aggregated Standard Traded Player Exception (100% + $250,000, simultaneous)
summary: A team can aggregate two or more Traded Players and bring back replacement contracts totaling up to 100% of their combined pre-trade salaries plus $250,000, acquired simultaneously.
detail_paraphrase: Subject to Section 2(e), a Team may use the Aggregated Standard Traded Player Exception to replace two or more Traded Players with one or more Replacement Players acquired simultaneously, whose post-trade Salaries for the then-current Salary Cap Year total no more than 100% of the aggregated pre-trade Salaries of the Traded Players plus $250,000.
conditions: Two or more Traded Players aggregated
Replacement Players acquired simultaneously
thresholds: Up to 100% of aggregated pre-trade Salaries plus $250,000
notes: Cross-reference: $250,000 allowance reduced to $0 above the First Apron Level (TRADE-029).

title: Transition Traded Player Exception (110% + $250,000, 2023-24 only)
summary: For the 2023-24 Salary Cap Year only, a team can bring back simultaneous replacement contracts totaling up to 110% of the traded players' pre-trade salaries plus $250,000.
detail_paraphrase: During the 2023-24 Salary Cap Year only, and subject to Section 2(e), a Team may use the Transition Traded Player Exception to replace one or more Traded Players with one or more Replacement Players acquired simultaneously, whose post-trade Salaries for 2023-24 total no more than 110% of the pre-trade Salaries of the Traded Players plus $250,000.
conditions: Trade occurs during the 2023-24 Salary Cap Year only
Replacement Players acquired simultaneously
thresholds: Up to 110% of pre-trade Salaries plus $250,000; 2023-24 only
notes: Cross-reference: $250,000 allowance reduced to $0 above the First Apron Level (TRADE-029).

title: Expanded Traded Player Exception (greater-of formula)
summary: A team can bring back simultaneous replacement salary up to the greater of three computed amounts based on 200%, a $7.5M-indexed band, or 125% of the aggregated pre-trade salaries (each plus $250,000 where applicable).
detail_paraphrase: Subject to Section 2(e), a Team may use the Expanded Traded Player Exception to replace one or more Traded Players with one or more Replacement Players acquired simultaneously, whose post-trade Salaries for the then-current Salary Cap Year total no more than the greater of: (y) the lesser of (A) 200% of the aggregated pre-trade Salaries plus $250,000, or (B) 100% of the aggregated pre-trade Salaries plus $7.5 million times the ratio of the current Salary Cap to the 2023-24 Salary Cap; or (z) 125% of the aggregated pre-trade Salaries plus $250,000.
conditions: Replacement Players acquired simultaneously
thresholds: Greater of: lesser of {200% + $250K, 100% + $7.5M-indexed}; or 125% + $250K of aggregated pre-trade Salaries
notes: Cross-reference: $250,000 allowance reduced to $0 above the First Apron Level (TRADE-029).

title: Room Under Salary Cap Plus $250,000 acquisition
summary: A team under the cap can acquire players whose post-assignment salaries total up to its cap room plus $250,000, but cannot combine this with the other Traded Player Exceptions.
detail_paraphrase: Except as provided in Section 6(j)(2), and notwithstanding Section 6(n), a Team below the Salary Cap may acquire one or more players by assignment whose post-assignment Salaries total no more than the Team's room under the Salary Cap plus $250,000. A Team acquiring players this way (or using room without the extra $250,000) may not simultaneously acquire any players under Sections 6(j)(1)(i)-(iv).
conditions: Team Salary is below the Salary Cap
exceptions: May not simultaneously combine with the Standard, Aggregated, Transition, or Expanded Traded Player Exceptions
thresholds: Cap room plus $250,000
notes: Cross-reference: $250,000 allowance reduced to $0 above the First Apron Level (TRADE-029).

title: Under-cap team may instead use Transition or Expanded TPE
summary: Instead of trading under the room-plus-$250,000 method, an under-cap team may conduct a trade using the Transition or Expanded Traded Player Exception.
detail_paraphrase: In lieu of conducting a trade under Section 6(j)(1)(v), and notwithstanding Section 6(n) but subject to Sections 2(e) and 6(j)(6), a Team below the Salary Cap may conduct a trade under Sections 6(j)(1)(iii)-(iv) (the Transition or Expanded Traded Player Exception).
conditions: Team Salary is below the Salary Cap
Team elects to use the Transition or Expanded TPE rather than room-plus-$250,000

title: Two-month aggregation restriction for recently acquired players
summary: A player acquired via an exception cannot be aggregated with other contracts in a trade until two months after he was acquired, with a December 16 carve-out for the trade deadline.
detail_paraphrase: When aggregating two or more Traded Players under the Aggregated, Transition, or Expanded Traded Player Exception, no player whose Contract was acquired pursuant to an Exception within the two-month period before the trade may be among the aggregated Traded Players. For example, a player acquired via an Exception on November 20, 2023 could not be aggregated until January 20, 2024. However, if a Team acquired a Player Contract via an Exception on or before December 16 of a Salary Cap Year, this restriction does not apply if the player is later traded on or after the day before that year's NBA trade deadline.
conditions: Player's Contract was acquired pursuant to an Exception
Team is aggregating two or more Traded Players under the Aggregated, Transition, or Expanded TPE
exceptions: Player acquired via Exception on or before December 16: restriction lifts for trades on or after the day before the trade deadline
thresholds: Two-month no-aggregation window; December 16 / trade-deadline carve-out

title: Minimum Traded Player aggregation limit (three-plus-player trades)
summary: Outside the December 15-to-trade-deadline window, when aggregating three or more Traded Players and acquiring fewer Replacement Players, at most one aggregated player may be a Minimum Traded Player.
detail_paraphrase: Other than during the period from December 15 through the NBA trade deadline of a Salary Cap Year, if a Team aggregates the Contracts of three or more Traded Players and acquires fewer Replacement Players than Traded Players, then no more than one of those Traded Players may be a Minimum Traded Player. A Minimum Traded Player is a player whose Contract provides his applicable Minimum Player Salary for the Salary Cap Year of the trade (or, for trades after the Regular Season through the end of the Salary Cap Year, his Minimum Player Salary for the immediately following Salary Cap Year).
conditions: Aggregating three or more Traded Players
Acquiring fewer Replacement Players than Traded Players
Trade occurs outside the December 15-to-trade-deadline window
exceptions: Restriction does not apply during the December 15 through NBA trade deadline period
thresholds: At most one Minimum Traded Player among aggregated players when replacements are fewer than traded players

title: Deemed outgoing salary for over-cap QFA/EQFA sign-and-trade (50% rule)
summary: For a sign-and-traded Bird free agent on an over-cap team whose new first-year salary exceeds the non-Bird amount, the assignor's outgoing trade-exception value is the greater of his prior salary or 50% of his new first-year salary.
detail_paraphrase: If a Qualifying or Early Qualifying Veteran Free Agent signs with his prior Team under Section 6(b)(1) or (3) in connection with an agreement to trade the Contract under Section 8(e), the Team's Team Salary right after the signing is above the Salary Cap, and the new Contract's first-season Salary plus Unlikely Bonuses exceed what could have been provided had the player been a Non-Qualifying Veteran Free Agent signed under Section 6(b)(2), then for calculating the assignor Team's Traded Player Exception the player's Salary is deemed to be the greater of (i) the Salary for the last Season of his preceding Contract or (ii) 50% of the first-season Salary of the new Contract. If the prior Contract was a one-year minimum-salary deal with no bonuses, the prior Salary includes any minimum reimbursed from the League-wide benefits fund.
conditions: QFA or EQFA signs with prior Team under Section 6(b)(1) or (3) for a sign-and-trade under Section 8(e)
Team Salary above the Salary Cap immediately after signing
New first-season Salary plus Unlikely Bonuses exceed the Non-Qualifying Veteran Free Agent amount
thresholds: Deemed outgoing Salary = greater of prior last-season Salary or 50% of new first-season Salary
notes: This is the 2023 CBA's functional replacement for the old Base Year Compensation concept for over-cap Bird sign-and-trades. See TRADE-031.

title: Outgoing salary reduced by unprotected Base Compensation; deadline-window protection deeming
summary: For trade-exception math, a traded player's salary is reduced by his unprotected unearned Base Compensation, with deeming rules treating that compensation as fully protected from January 8 through season's end and special lesser-of treatment after the season.
detail_paraphrase: When calculating a Team's Traded Player Exception, a Traded Player's Salary is deemed reduced by the unearned Base Compensation that, at the time of the trade, is not fully protected for lack of skill and injury/illness (or could become unprotected due to Exhibit 2 conditions). For assignments from January 8 through the last day of the Regular Season, a Traded Player's Base Compensation for that Season is deemed fully protected. For a one-year minimum-salary contract (no bonuses), unearned Base Compensation excludes any minimum reimbursed from the League-wide benefits fund. For assignments from the day after the Regular Season through June 30, the Traded Player's Salary equals the lesser of his current-year Salary and his next-year Salary reduced by next-year unprotected unearned Base Compensation. The CBA illustrates these with an $8M/$1M-protected example yielding $1M, $2M, $8M, and $1M outgoing values at four trade dates.
conditions: Calculating a Team's Traded Player Exception for a Traded Player with unprotected unearned Base Compensation
exceptions: January 8 through end of Regular Season: that Season's Base Compensation deemed fully protected
Day after Regular Season through June 30: lesser-of current-year vs. reduced next-year Salary applies
thresholds: Outgoing Salary reduced by unprotected unearned Base Compensation; January 8 protection-deeming date

title: No TPE from a player covered by a Disabled Player Exception
summary: No Traded Player Exception arises from trading a player for whom the team has used or simultaneously uses a Disabled Player Exception that Salary Cap Year.
detail_paraphrase: Notwithstanding the rest of Section 6(j), no Traded Player Exception arises from trading a player during a Salary Cap Year if the Team has previously used, or simultaneously uses, a Disabled Player Exception in respect of that player during the same Salary Cap Year.
conditions: Team has used or simultaneously uses a Disabled Player Exception for the same player in the same Salary Cap Year

title: Traded Player Exceptions do not apply to Two-Way Players
summary: No Traded Player Exception arises from trading a Two-Way Player; the Section 6(j) rules do not apply to Two-Way Players.
detail_paraphrase: The rules in Section 6(j) do not apply to Two-Way Players. Accordingly, no Traded Player Exception arises from trading a Two-Way Player.
conditions: Player being traded is a Two-Way Player

title: $250,000 trade allowance eliminated above the First Apron
summary: If a team's post-assignment Apron Team Salary would exceed the First Apron Level, the $250,000 allowance in every Traded Player Exception is reduced to $0.
detail_paraphrase: Notwithstanding Section 6(j)(1), if a Team's post-assignment Apron Team Salary would exceed the First Apron Level, the $250,000 allowance referenced in each of Sections 6(j)(1)(i) through (v) is reduced to $0.
conditions: Team's post-assignment Apron Team Salary would exceed the First Apron Level
thresholds: $250,000 allowance reduced to $0 above the First Apron Level
notes: Cross-reference: full apron-based trade restrictions are in the aprons bucket; this captures only the base $250,000 interaction.

title: Traded Player Exception eligibility and Team Salary inclusion (Section 6(n))
summary: A TPE may be used only while the team is at/above the cap or below it by less than the exception amount; an unused TPE is added into Team Salary until used or expired.
detail_paraphrase: A Team may use a Traded Player Exception (among the listed exceptions) only if, when the exception arises and at all times until used, the Team's Team Salary—excluding the exception amounts—is at or above the Salary Cap or below it by less than the exception amount(s). When such an exception arises while Team Salary is below the Cap by less than the exception amount, the Team's Team Salary includes the exception (or unused portion) until it is used or the Team can no longer use it, extinguishing the gap below the Cap. When the exception is used to acquire a player, the acquired Contract's then-current-year Salary plus any unused portion of the exception is included in Team Salary instead of the full exception. A Team may renounce an exception at any time, removing it (or its unused portion) from Team Salary. The room-plus-$250,000 method (6(j)(1)(v)) and 6(j)(2) are excepted from these eligibility constraints.
conditions: Team seeks to use a Traded Player Exception (other than the room-plus-$250,000 method under 6(j)(1)(v) or 6(j)(2))
exceptions: Sections 6(j)(1)(v) and 6(j)(2) are excepted from the Section 6(n)(1) eligibility test
thresholds: Eligibility tied to Team Salary being at/above the Cap or below it by less than the exception amount

title: Base Year Compensation not present in the 2023 CBA
summary: The term 'Base Year Compensation' does not appear in the provided 2023 CBA text; its prior salary-matching function for over-cap Bird sign-and-trades is now handled by the Section 6(j)(5) deemed-salary (50%) rule.
detail_paraphrase: The task scope lists Base Year Compensation as living in Article VII, Section 3, but the term does not appear in the provided Section 3 text or anywhere else in the supplied 2023 CBA work files. The functional analogue for over-cap Qualifying/Early Qualifying Veteran Free Agent sign-and-trades is the Section 6(j)(5) rule, which deems the outgoing player's Salary for Traded Player Exception purposes to be the greater of his prior last-season Salary or 50% of his new first-season Salary. This rule object flags the absence so compliance logic does not rely on a defined 'Base Year Compensation' term that the 2023 CBA does not use.
notes: REVIEW: 'Base Year Compensation' is absent from the provided Section 3 (Determination of Salary) text and from a full-text search of the supplied CBA files. The 2023 CBA appears not to use this term; Section 6(j)(5) is its functional replacement (see TRADE-025). Verify against the official executed CBA before relying on any BYC definition.

title: Signing bonus and trade bonus treated as signing-bonus salary on a trade
summary: For salary determination, a bonus earned upon the trade of a contract is treated as a signing bonus and allocated over the then-current and remaining Salary Cap Years per the proration rules.
detail_paraphrase: For determining a player's Salary, the term signing bonus includes any amount that, under the Contract's terms, is earned as a bonus upon the trade of the Contract (i.e., a trade bonus). Such an amount is allocated over the then-current and remaining Salary Cap Years of the Contract in proportion to the Base Compensation in each year protected for lack of skill; if none is protected, the entire amount is allocated to the Salary Cap Year in which the Contract is traded.
conditions: A Player Contract containing a bonus earned upon its trade is traded
thresholds: Allocated over then-current and remaining Salary Cap Years by protected Base Compensation share

title: Trade bonus permitted (15% cap, first-trade-only, paid once)
summary: A contract may include a trade bonus payable only the first time it is traded, capped at 15% of remaining Base Compensation, and never payable more than once.
detail_paraphrase: A Player Contract may include (in Exhibit 4) a trade bonus entitling the player to earn Compensation if his Contract is traded. The bonus is payable only the first time the Contract is traded; but if the Contract was signed in connection with a Section 8(e) sign-and-trade, the bonus does not apply to that initial trade and is instead payable only the second time the Contract is traded. A trade bonus may not exceed 15% of the Base Compensation remaining to be earned at the time of the trade (excluding an unexercised Option Year). In no event may a trade bonus be payable more than once.
conditions: Contract contains an Exhibit 4 trade bonus
Contract is traded
exceptions: Section 8(e) sign-and-trade: bonus applies to the second trade, not the initial trade
thresholds: Trade bonus capped at 15% of remaining Base Compensation; payable once only

title: Trade bonus amendment and addition rules
summary: Trade bonuses may be modified or removed in limited ways via extensions or trades; a contract without one may add one only at extension, and only a replacement Exhibit 4 may waive it for the extended term.
detail_paraphrase: Exhibit 4 may be amended only as specified: to set the bonus amount (a percentage of remaining Base Compensation excluding an unexercised Option Year, or a dollar amount not exceeding such a percentage); in connection with an Extension, to modify the amount (subject to the 15% cap) or to make the bonus inapplicable to the extended term; in connection with a Section 8(e) sign-and-trade Extension, to reduce the amount or make it inapplicable to the extended term; or in connection with a trade (other than a sign-and-trade), to reduce the amount. A Contract without a trade bonus when signed cannot add one except via an Extension—payable only the first time traded after the Extension (or, for a Section 8(e) sign-and-trade Extension, only on a second trade). If an Extension makes an unearned trade bonus inapplicable to the extended term, the Extension must include a replacement Exhibit 4 with the original terms plus a statement that the bonus does not apply to the extended term.
conditions: Amendment, extension, or trade affecting an Exhibit 4 trade bonus
exceptions: A Contract without a trade bonus may add one only via an Extension, with the stated timing limits
thresholds: Modifications subject to the 15% remaining-Base-Compensation cap

title: General prohibition of no-trade contracts
summary: No Player Contract may prohibit or limit a Team's right to assign the contract to another Team, except where Article XXIV permits.
detail_paraphrase: As a general rule, no Player Contract may contain any prohibition or limitation on an NBA Team's right to assign that Contract to another NBA Team. This general limitation is subject to the exceptions set out in Article XXIV, Section 2 (the trade bonus and the permitted veteran no-trade clause).
conditions: A Player Contract purports to prohibit or limit assignment to another Team
exceptions: Permitted trade bonus (Section 2(a))
Permitted veteran no-trade clause (Section 2(b))

title: Permitted no-trade clause for 8/4 veterans
summary: A player with 8+ Years of Service in the NBA and 4+ Years of Service for the signing Team may include a no-trade clause in that contract.
detail_paraphrase: A Player Contract entered into by a player who has at least eight Years of Service in the NBA and has rendered at least four Years of Service for the Team entering into the Contract may contain a prohibition or limitation on that Team's right to trade the Contract to another NBA Team.
conditions: Player has 8 or more Years of Service in the NBA
Player has rendered 4 or more Years of Service for the Team entering into the Contract
thresholds: 8+ Years of Service in the NBA and 4+ Years of Service for the signing Team

title: Anti-circumvention prohibition applies to trades and assignments
summary: Teams and players may not structure a trade, assignment, or contract amendment to circumvent the CBA's salary-cap and related intentions; violations carry fines, pick forfeiture, and voiding.
detail_paraphrase: No Team, Team Affiliate, or player may enter any agreement—including any Player Contract, Renegotiation, Extension, or amendment—or undertake any action or transaction, including the assignment or termination of a Player Contract, that is designed to defeat or circumvent the intentions reflected by the CBA's provisions (Salary Cap, exceptions, BRI, escrow/tax, Rookie Scale, Right of First Refusal, Maximum Player Salary, and free agency). Upon a System Arbitrator finding (after any appeal), the Commissioner may fine a Team up to $4.5M (first violation) or $5.5M (repeat), direct forfeiture of a first-round pick, void the offending contract or transaction, and void any other transaction found to violate the section.
conditions: An agreement, assignment, termination, or transaction is designed to defeat or circumvent the CBA's intentions
thresholds: Fines up to $4.5M (first) / $5.5M (repeat); first-round pick forfeiture; voiding
notes: Penalties summarized from Article XIII, Section 3(a) (printed pp.341-342).

title: Poison-pill provision not present under that label
summary: No 'poison pill' provision appears in the provided trade-scope CBA files; the closest analogues (sign-and-trade deemed salary, offer-sheet matching) live elsewhere.
detail_paraphrase: A full-text search of the provided 2023 CBA work files found no 'poison pill' term in Article VII Sections 3, 6, or 8, in Article XXIV, or in Article XIII. The commonly referenced 'poison pill' mechanics relate to (a) the sign-and-trade deemed-salary treatment captured in Section 6(j)(5) (see TRADE-025) and (b) offer-sheet salary structuring under Article XI free agency, which is outside the trades bucket source files. This rule flags that there is no separately labeled poison-pill trade rule to extract from the supplied sources.
notes: REVIEW: 'Poison pill' is absent from all provided source files. If a poison-pill rule is required, its mechanics derive from Article XI (offer sheets, free agency bucket) and Section 6(j)(5) deemed salary, neither labeled 'poison pill' in the 2023 CBA. Confirm scope intent.
